sentiment.rationale: Johnson & Johnson raised its full-year 2025 reported sales guidance by $2 billion to a midpoint of $93.4 billion (5.4% growth) and raised adjusted EPS guidance by $0.25 to $10.85, citing strong operational performance and favorable FX. The guidance raise is meaningful and driven by both operational strength and currency tailwinds, with management expressing high confidence in accelerating second-half growth. While FX contributed $1.1 billion to the sales raise and $0.17 to EPS, the core operational guidance also increased (operational sales midpoint up $0.9B, adjusted operational EPS up $0.08), supporting a score above +0.5 but not at the maximum due to the FX attribution and ongoing STELARA erosion.

summary.revenue: Q2 2025 reported sales of $23,743 million, up 5.8% year-over-year; operational growth 4.6%; adjusted operational growth 3.0%.
summary.eps: Q2 2025 diluted EPS of $2.29, up 18.7% year-over-year; adjusted diluted EPS of $2.77, down 1.8% year-over-year.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025 guidance raised: reported sales midpoint $93.4B (5.4% growth, up from $91.4B/3.1%); operational sales midpoint $92.9B (4.8% growth, up from $92.0B/3.8%); adjusted EPS midpoint $10.85 (8.7% growth, up from $10.60/6.2%); adjusted operational EPS midpoint $10.68 (7.0% growth, up from $10.60/6.2%).
summary.margin: Q2 2025 gross margin (GAAP) was 67.9% (gross profit $16,115M on sales $23,743M), down from 69.4% in Q2 2024. Adjusted segment income before tax margin for Innovative Medicine declined from 44.6% to 42.7%; MedTech declined from 25.7% to 22.2%. Management reiterated full-year operating margin improvement of ~300 bps.
key_risks: STELARA biosimilar competition and Part D redesign causing significant erosion (43.2% decline in Q2, ~1,170 bps headwind to Innovative Medicine growth).
Ongoing talc litigation with Daubert hearing expected in fall 2025.
Tariff impact on MedTech business estimated at ~$200 million for 2025.
Competitive pressures in orthopaedics, energy, and electrophysiology PFA.
China VBP (volume-based procurement) negatively impacting MedTech and orthopaedics.
Part D redesign negatively impacting multiple products including STELARA, INVEGA, ERLEADA, OPSUMIT, UPTRAVI, TREMFYA, IMBRUVICA.
key_opportunities: TAR-200 for non-muscle invasive bladder cancer with FDA priority review, expected launch later this year, peak sales potential at least $5 billion.
CARVYKTI growth over 100% in Q2 with capacity expansion and five-year remission data.
RYBREVANT/LAZCLUZE launch momentum with over 100% growth and potential to become standard of care in frontline EGFR-mutated NSCLC.
TREMFYA growth of 30% with IBD expansion, peak sales potential at least $10 billion.
CAPLYTA acquisition (Intra-Cellular) adding $5B+ peak sales potential and MDD approval anticipated later this year.
MedTech cardiovascular growth of 22% driven by Abiomed, Shockwave, and electrophysiology.
OTTAVA robotic surgical system progressing toward FDA de novo submission next year.
Icotrokinra, first targeted oral peptide for IL-23 receptor, expected FDA filing in Q3 2025.
Vision growth with ACUVUE OASYS MAX and TECNIS Odyssey.
